notes: Main problem: any .gov/.edu page ranks high even when it isn't useful content (catalogue records, event and course pages, program marketing, staging copies).
The same document hosted twice (SWEBOK 2004 on two sites) and same-title pages on one host count twice.
The real authorities per domain are missing (e.g. Cornell LII, Nolo and the ABA for legal; EEOC, SHRM and DOL for HR; Google SRE, PagerDuty and Atlassian for incidents).
github.com/google/eng-practices was wrongly rejected for software-engineering.
hr/recruiting fails: junk in the top 5 (#1 is DOL's own job application page).
marketing/strategy fails: #1-2 are FTC pages titled only "www.ftc.gov" (content unknown); #8 is an EPA volunteer-program page.
legal/contracts fails: #3 is an ABA index page, #4 GOV.UK transparency data, #5 a Pembrokeshire FOI disclosure, #10 a CBCA page on an ABA manual.

Search alone can't reach some authority pages: pin verified sources per domain, block careers, FOI, transparency-data and link-index pages, fetch real titles for pages titled only by their host, and rank US sources first for legal/contracts.
technology/ai fails: #9 is an Atlassian course, #10 a Medium post, #6 an Idaho page with 0 topic words.
legal/contracts fails: junk in the top 5 (#5 cbca.gov ABA manual); #4, #6 and #10 are crawl: no.

Last round, general rules only: non-pinned sources need at least 1 topic word; crawl: no sources leave the top 10 for a separate list; unknown-tier and off-area sources need a pin; pin 2-3 sources for technology/ai; label known federal .gov hosts US (federal).
